target.title: feat: keep reset session history searchable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resetting a SQLite-backed session currently deletes its old transcript and trajectory history, so a reset also erases searchable context. Session disk-budget accounting also omits the SQLite database and WAL, making the configured physical limit incomplete.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reset now advances the live session ID while retaining the old SQLite rows and search projections. Explicit deletion remains archive-then-delete and removes every retained generation for the deleted key.

Disk accounting measures physical session artifacts plus the agent SQLite main file and WAL. Enforced cleanup extracts historical sessions oldest-first to the existing compressed archive format, fsyncs and reads the archive back, then deletes database rows through the lifecycle transaction helpers and physically remeasures after checkpoint/incremental-vacuum work. Live entry references, route targets, and admitted/in-flight session identities are excluded; trajectory-only sessions remain eligible.

No DDL, schema-version change, config key, legacy JSONL migration, legacy file-store change, or vacuum-into rewrite is included. The existing schema and cascade/projection cleanup surfaces are sufficient.

## User Impact

After reset, only the new live session appears in entry/list views, while pre-reset content remains searchable under the same session key. When physical session storage exceeds the configured maximum, explicit cleanup can extract unreferenced history before removing it from SQLite and stops at the high-water target. Warn mode reports without eviction.

This is a user-visible retention change. Per contributor policy, this PR intentionally does not edit `CHANGELOG.md`; maintainers should include the release-note context when landing.

## Evidence

All proof ran locally in the task worktree; no remote Testbox or delegated implementation was used.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/store.session-lifecycle-mutation.test.ts` — 13 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-history-eviction.test.ts` — 4 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/store.pruning.integration.test.ts` — 41 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/disk-budget.test.ts` — 20 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed

No-DDL proof: the change does not modify canonical schema files, migrations, schema-version constants, or generated schema artifacts. It only queries and deletes existing session/event/projection rows through current helpers.

Extract-then-evict invariant: each historical victim is archived, fsynced, read back, and verified before the SQLite deletion transaction begins. The deletion rechecks live/route/admission protection and uses the lifecycle cleanup path for transcript, trajectory, active, index, and FTS projections.

Admission-exclusion boundary: cleanup combines live entry references, route-target references, and the active-work admission set; admitted keys are resolved through both live entry and SQLite state IDs before candidate selection and are rechecked under the lifecycle fence.

### Draft blockers after the frozen two-cycle autoreview limit

This PR is intentionally left draft. Two convergence cycles were allowed; the final reviews still found these issues:

1. Serialize retained-archive pruning with lifecycle deletion so a concurrent cleanup cannot unlink a newly verified archive before its row-deletion transaction.
2. Restore a physical budget-enforcement trigger in ordinary session maintenance, not only explicit `runSessionsCleanup` calls.
3. Re-run archive-tier pruning after each new historical archive before evicting another SQLite session, avoiding unnecessary over-eviction when database bytes do not shrink immediately.
4. Include checkpoint/incremental-vacuum-only work in preview and applied mutation reporting.

AI-assisted implementation and review were used. All resulting source changes and proof were inspected and executed in the local checkout.
